doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: Chasing record labels and drifting into session work
summary: He went to L.A. wanting to be in a creative band and chase a label deal; lack of interest pushed him toward session and touring work, and bandmates faced the same pull.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: We might as well — we can go there now. Because right on my page here I have “record labels.” And I wanted to ask what that was like because in the 80s I was in a band that was trying for that. There’s this term that we I think probably you’ve used too in the back of your mind like, “I want to make it big.” “I want to make it in the music business.” And it used to be all right, you have to hook up with a record label.

Right, right. Well that used to be true. And certainly still in the late 70s when I got there and into the early 80s that was true. And it’s funny because I really went to L.A., I didn’t really have any interest in becoming a session player or a touring musician. I wanted to be part of a creative force, be part of a band. And I wanted to be involved in, hopefully, the writing, the singing and the playing — whether it was bass guitar or whatever. But that was my central focus. And it was only out of really necessity after years of trying to get record label interest in these various projects that I kind of went man, this is not quite working as I had hoped. And then fortunately things started coming, session work was coming and touring work, and I was able to survive as a working musician, which at that point I was really thrilled about. And I’ve always been thrilled about. So I kind of put that group thing, at one point it was just financially I had to move it over here and then kind of go over here to survive.
Were your bandmates experiencing the same kind of situation?

Yeah. Absolutely. And one of the reasons these bands were so tough to keep together, the players were good and they were being offered touring gigs and they were being offered other things. So keeping a working entity together was tough because there were all these other offers coming in and that just kind of added to the equation of like doing a band was really, really hard.
